<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915661_theRebbe_783" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915661_theRebbe_783__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the phrase "Your pious ones will bless You" means they draw down a revelation into Malchus specifically from the level of Ein Sof that is beyond comprehension, where only acknowledgment (Hoda'ah) applies.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood by prefacing what is said</t>
    <t s="2">"All Your works shall praise You, and Your pious ones will bless You,"</t>
    <t s="3">and it is brought in the Zohar</t>
    <t s="4">that the explanation of "will bless You" (yevarchuchah) is "they will bless *koh*."</t>
    <t s="5">And the Rebbe</t>
    <t s="6">(the Rebbe Rashab)</t>
    <t s="7">of blessed memory</t>
    <t s="8">(in his maamar beginning "Padeh b'Shalom" from the year 5668),</t>
    <t s="9">explains that *koh* is Malchus,</t>
    <t s="10">and "they will bless *koh*" means to draw down a revelation of light into Malchus.</t>
    <t s="11">And it is stated "and Your pious ones will bless You,"</t>
    <t s="12">that this drawing down is specifically through the power of "Your pious ones."</t>
    <t s="13">And the explanation is,</t>
    <t s="14">that this matter of "Your pious ones will bless You" is in proximity and continuation to "All Your works shall praise You,"</t>
    <t s="15">that is,</t>
    <t s="16">because the drawing down into Malchus</t>
    <t s="17">(which is through "Your pious ones")</t>
    <t s="18">is from a very exalted place</t>
    <t s="19">(the Ein Sof that is above the chain of descent)</t>
    <t s="20">regarding which comprehension does not apply, only acknowledgment (Hoda'ah) alone,</t>
    <t s="21">"they will praise You."</t>
    <t s="22">And the drawing down from there</t>
    <t s="23">(in the manner of blessing)</t>
    <t s="24">is specifically through the power of "Your pious ones."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section distinguishes between prayer (from below to above, requesting new light) and blessing (from above to below, commanding an existing flow), noting that prayer can draw a new will from Ein Sof while blessing is a certain command.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And in order to understand the great superiority of the drawing down in the manner of blessing from the place where there is acknowledgment (Hoda'ah),</t>
    <t s="1">the maamar prefaces the distinction between blessing and prayer,</t>
    <t s="2">that in each one there is an advantage over the other.</t>
    <t s="3">And the explanation is,</t>
    <t s="4">that prayer is from below to above,</t>
    <t s="5">meaning that the one praying is below and requests that they bestow upon him from above,</t>
    <t s="6">and blessing is from above to below,</t>
    <t s="7">that the one who blesses is above the source from which the blessing is drawn, and he draws it from above to below.</t>
    <t s="8">And this is that blessing is in the manner of a command,</t>
    <t s="9">for since the one who blesses is above the source from which the blessing is drawn,</t>
    <t s="10">therefore he has the power to command.</t>
    <t s="11">And this is that blessing is specifically for one who has the power to bless</t>
    <t s="12">(like Avraham Avinu, to whom the Holy One, blessed be He, said "the blessings are given to you"),</t>
    <t s="13">[and unlike prayer, which anyone can pray,</t>
    <t s="14">and moreover, everyone is commanded to pray],</t>
    <t s="15">because in order to bless,</t>
    <t s="16">the one who blesses must be above the source from which the blessing is drawn.</t>
    <t s="17">And from this the advantage of blessing over prayer is understood,</t>
    <t s="18">for in prayer,</t>
    <t s="19">which is a request that they draw down the influence,</t>
    <t s="20">there is no certainty that the request will be fulfilled.</t>
    <t s="21">But in blessing, which is in the manner of a command—the influence will certainly be drawn down,</t>
    <t s="22">since the one who blesses has the power to command.</t>
    <t s="23">And the advantage of prayer over blessing is in the drawing down itself,</t>
    <t s="24">that the drawing down through prayer is more exalted.</t>
    <t s="25">For the matter of blessing is to draw down what already exists in the source, and not something new,</t>
    <t s="26">and the matter of prayer is a request from the Holy One, blessed be He, that even if the influence is not changed even in the source, heaven forbid,</t>
    <t s="27">and moreover, even if it has been decreed upon him that he should be ill, heaven forbid, and the like,</t>
    <t s="28">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="29">a new influence will be drawn down to him from the Ein Sof that is above the chain of descent.</t>
    <t s="30">For this is what is said in several prayers, "May it be His will" (Yehi Ratzon),</t>
    <t s="31">that the explanation of "May it be His will" is that there should be a new will.</t>
    <t s="32">And the reason for this, that the drawing down of a new light is specifically through prayer,</t>
    <t s="33">is "for You desire the work of Your hands,"</t>
    <t s="34">and therefore,</t>
    <t s="35">through prayer,</t>
    <t s="36">the work of the one below,</t>
    <t s="37">they reach the Ein Sof that is above the chain of descent.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the blessing of the pious ones combines both advantages: it draws a new will from Ein Sof (like prayer) yet is issued as a command (like blessing), as seen in the Jerusalem Talmud about a righteous person's decree overriding G-d's.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And based on this, the great superiority of the blessing</t>
    <t s="1">(of "Your pious ones")</t>
    <t s="2">is understood, that its drawing down is from the place where there is acknowledgment (Hoda'ah),</t>
    <t s="3">for in this blessing there are both advantages.</t>
    <t s="4">That the drawing down is from the Ein Sof that is above the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="5">meaning that through this blessing a new will is made—the advantage of prayer.</t>
    <t s="6">And nevertheless it is</t>
    <t s="7">(not prayer,</t>
    <t s="8">a request,</t>
    <t s="9">but rather)</t>
    <t s="10">a blessing,</t>
    <t s="11">in the manner of a command.</t>
    <t s="12">And this is similar to what is brought in the Jerusalem Talmud</t>
    <t s="13">on the verse</t>
    <t s="14">"And you shall decree a thing, and it will be established for you,"</t>
    <t s="15">that even if He</t>
    <t s="16">(the Holy One, blessed be He)</t>
    <t s="17">says "thus" and you say "thus,"</t>
    <t s="18">yours stands and Mine does not stand.</t>
    <t s="19">For this, that the Holy One, blessed be He, nullifies His decree because of the decree of the righteous person,</t>
    <t s="20">is</t>
    <t s="21">because the righteous person draws down a new will—the advantage of prayer,</t>
    <t s="22">and the manner of the nullification of the decree is</t>
    <t s="23">(not through a request,</t>
    <t s="24">but rather)</t>
    <t s="25">through the decree of the righteous person—the advantage of blessing, which is in the manner of a command.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
